per_pair.why: Vibrant color palette and pronounced visual effects make the combo progression read clearly throughout the sequence.
Colorful character design and enhanced visual feedback create stronger impact sensation than A's muted, text-heavy approach.
Large, dramatic knockback creature sprite provides immediate visceral impact that makes the finisher feel heavy and satisfying.

loser_biggest_gap: Add dramatic visual feedback effects like knockback sprites or screen-space effects to convey impact weight; the text-based feedback and muted palette make hits feel weightless.
loser_other_gaps: Expand the color palette to differentiate hits, effects, and environmental feedback - muted tones blend together and reduce readability
Include prominent screen-space effects or particles on finishers to create visual punctuation for combo payoff moments
Refine character and enemy silhouettes to match B's clarity and visual appeal
reasoning: Game B delivers heavier, more satisfying hits through superior visual communication. The colorful, differentiated palette makes effects immediately readable. Pair 03 demonstrates this gap most clearly: B's massive knockback creature sprite provides visceral feedback that A's scattered damage numbers cannot match. B's animation spacing and sprite design also feel more polished and weighty. The gap is clear but not decisive - A functions well but lacks the visual craft and feedback intensity of a polished indie game.
